releases.notes:
**Birds from Finally More Biomes and Mo Creatures no longer swap models when both mods are installed.**

## Bird model clash with Mo Creatures

Finally More Biomes and Mo Creatures both gave their bird model the same name. The game only keeps
one model per name, so whichever mod loaded last decided what both birds looked like. Finally More
Biomes' models now have names of their own, so each mod's bird looks the way it should.

## Install

**Requires** Better than Adventure! `8.0.1`. HalpLibe is bundled inside the jar, so there is nothing
else to download.

releases.notes:
**Items from other mods no longer go missing from the creative inventory because of Finally More Biomes.**

## Missing creative items from other mods

Finally More Biomes checked its own creative inventory entries while the game was starting, and that
check made the creative inventory fill up earlier than it normally would. The creative inventory is
only filled once, so a mod that adds its items later during startup found it already done, and its
items never showed up: not in the creative inventory, and not in Too Many Blocks, which shows the same
list. Better With Aether 1.1.2-pre2 is one of those mods.

The check now waits until the game fills the creative inventory by itself, so Finally More Biomes no
longer changes what ends up in it.

## If you also use Too Many Blocks

Too Many Blocks reads the creative inventory even earlier during startup, on its own. With it
installed, Better With Aether 1.1.2-pre2's items can still be missing whether or not this mod is
there. A fix for that has to come from one of those two mods.

## Install

**Requires** Better than Adventure! `8.0.1`. HalpLibe is bundled inside the jar, so there is nothing
else to download.

releases.notes:
**Two new overworlds that share the world with BTA's biomes, and two that are amplified.**

## The old world type said "woven" and was not

`Finally More Biomes` put its own biomes in the overworld *in place of* BTA's — none of BTA's forty-one
were in its climate table at all — while its description in the Create World screen read "Finally
More Biomes's biomes, woven into the overworld." That description now says what it does: an overworld
of Finally More Biomes's own biomes in place of BTA's. The world type itself is unchanged, so a world
you are already playing keeps generating exactly as it started.

## FMB Woven

The one the old description was describing. Both rosters share one overworld: the land is split
between them in proportion to their size, so a biome from either turns up about as often as it would
in a world of its own kind, and each roster keeps its own internal arrangement rather than being
squeezed into a corner of the other's.

The sea stays as Finally More Biomes has it, whole. Its coastlines and ocean biomes already work and
the surface rules are written against them; a second set of shores in the same water would not have
improved anything.

## FMB Amplified, and FMB Woven Amplified

The same two rosters on terrain stretched across the full height of the world with the sea left low.
Mountains reach the clouds and the caves go a long way down. Everything else is identical — same
biomes, same trees, same decoration.

## One thing worth knowing

The woven types are new geometry, so they are their own entries rather than a change to the existing
one. Four Finally More Biomes overworlds now appear when you create a world; all four keep the mod's
Nether and the Promised Land.

## Install

**Requires** Better than Adventure! `8.0.1`. HalpLibe is bundled inside the jar, so there is nothing
else to download.

Download `betteroplenty-0.1.16+8.0.1.jar` and drop it in your instance's `.minecraft/mods/` folder.

releases.notes:
Finally More Biomes now shares a world properly with other mods that add dimensions.

## If you play with the Aether, this is the one to update to

Both mods wanted the same dimension slot, and the Aether always got there first. What that cost was not obvious. The Promised Land became unreachable, which is the part you would notice — and then, much more quietly, the Biomes O' Plenty world type vanished from the Create World screen, this mod's mob sounds went silent, its recipes stopped working and its achievements stopped firing. All of it from one number.

It was not really the Aether's doing, or this mod's. There are only so many dimension slots, the first free one is the obvious choice, and every mod that adds a dimension reaches for it.

This release takes the first slot nobody else is using, and remembers which one it took. It will not move again in that installation, so a world you build today keeps its Promised Land where it left it even if you add or remove other mods later.

## And a second problem underneath it

With enough dimension mods installed, the slots stop being consecutive — one mod takes a number well above the others and leaves a gap in between. The game cannot cope with a gap. The list of world types every mod builds falls over the moment it meets one, and it takes whatever mod happened to be building at that moment down with it.

That is what was actually happening in the report that started this, and it is why so much more than the Promised Land went missing. This release works around it, for its own world types and for the game's built-in ones, so a pack with a gap in its dimension numbering starts and plays normally.

When something does go wrong now, the log says which slots are missing and which mod holds what, instead of one bare line.

## One thing worth knowing

If you already have a world with a Promised Land in it and you have since added another dimension mod, that old Promised Land cannot be reached any more — its slot belongs to something else. The log will say so and name the world. Removing the other mod puts it back exactly as it was; nothing is deleted either way.

## Install

Drop `betteroplenty-0.1.15+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. Drop-in replacement for 0.1.14.

releases.notes:
All seven of this port's mobs are now in the guidebook.

## The mobs are in the guidebook

Open the guidebook and the Creatures section runs on past BTA's own animals into the jungle spider, the rosester, the bird, the wasp, the pixie, the glob and the phantom — each with its picture, its health, what it drops and a line or two about what it is.

Nothing was broken before. Adding a mob to the game and adding it to the book are two separate things, and only the first had ever been done, so the pages simply did not exist. The names were already translated; the descriptions beside them are new.

Four of the seven cannot be met by chance — the bird and the phantom belong to dimensions this port has not built yet, the pixie's home is still an open question, and the wasp has never had a spawn in any version of the mod. They have pages anyway. A mob you can only reach with a spawn egg is the one you are most likely to want the book for.

The phantom's page shows an empty picture box, and that is correct: it is the one mob in the mod that is deliberately never drawn. Its description says so.

The figures on each page are read off a live mob rather than typed out by hand — the jungle spider's 6 health against a common spider's 16, the glob's mudballs, the rosester's red dye — so a page cannot quietly go stale when a mob changes.

Nothing about how any of them behave has changed. This is the book only.

## Install

Drop `betteroplenty-0.1.14+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. Drop-in replacement for 0.1.13.
